objects.definition: typedef uint8_t  PCRE2_UCHAR8;
objects.description: 8-bit code unit type used by PCRE2 for pattern and subject strings when compiled for 8-bit width.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t PCRE2_UCHAR16;
objects.description: 16-bit code unit type used by PCRE2 for pattern and subject strings when compiled for 16-bit width.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t PCRE2_UCHAR32;
objects.description: 32-bit code unit type used by PCRE2 for pattern and subject strings when compiled for 32-bit width.

objects.definition: typedef const PCRE2_UCHAR8  *PCRE2_SPTR8;
objects.description: Pointer-to-const 8-bit code unit string type for PCRE2 APIs (8-bit mode).

objects.definition: typedef const PCRE2_UCHAR16 *PCRE2_SPTR16;
objects.description: Pointer-to-const 16-bit code unit string type for PCRE2 APIs (16-bit mode).

objects.definition: typedef const PCRE2_UCHAR32 *PCRE2_SPTR32;
objects.description: Pointer-to-const 32-bit code unit string type for PCRE2 APIs (32-bit mode).

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_general_context; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_general_context pcre2_general_context;
objects.description: Opaque context object holding general allocation and library-global settings for PCRE2.

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_compile_context; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_compile_context pcre2_compile_context;
objects.description: Opaque context object controlling compile-time options and limits for compiling patterns.

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_match_context; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_match_context pcre2_match_context;
objects.description: Opaque context object controlling match-time behavior such as limits, callouts, JIT stack assignment.

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_convert_context; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_convert_context pcre2_convert_context;
objects.description: Opaque context object controlling behavior of pattern source conversion utilities (glob/POSIX/basic, etc.).

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_code; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_code pcre2_code;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a compiled regular expression pattern (optionally JIT-compiled). Must be freed with pcre2_code_free.

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_match_data; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_match_data pcre2_match_data;
objects.description: Opaque match result container holding ovector and auxiliary data from a match. Free with pcre2_match_data_free.

objects.definition:
struct pcre2_real_jit_stack; 
typedef struct pcre2_real_jit_stack pcre2_jit_stack;
objects.description: Opaque JIT stack resource used by JIT-compiled matching. Create with pcre2_jit_stack_create, free with pcre2_jit_stack_free.

objects.definition: typedef pcre2_jit_stack *(*pcre2_jit_callback)(void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks that supply a pcre2_jit_stack*. Typically assigned via pcre2_jit_stack_assign.
Data block passed to user callout functions during matching. Contains subject, offsets, capture info, and optional callout string and flags.
Data provided to the enumeration callback from pcre2_callout_enumerate to describe callouts in a pattern.
Data passed to the substitute callout during pcre2_substitute, exposing input/output slices and current ovector.
POSIX wrapper structure for a compiled PCRE2 regex plus execution/match storage and flags, used with regcomp/regexec APIs.

objects.definition: typedef int regoff_t;
objects.description: POSIX wrapper type for a submatch offset integer, used within regmatch_t.
POSIX wrapper structure returning one captured substring’s start and end offsets.

functions.name: pcre2_config
functions.description: Queries library/build configuration information (e.g., version string, Unicode support) and writes the result to the buffer pointed to by where, based on the request code in what. Intended for applications to discover PCRE2 build-time characteristics.
requirements: what must be one of the PCRE2_CONFIG_* constants defined in the header.
where must point to writable storage appropriate for the requested item’s type/size (unknown from header; consult PCRE2 docs for exact sizes).
The function returns a status code; callers should check the return value for success or failure.

functions.name: pcre2_general_context_copy
functions.description: Creates a new general-context by copying an existing general-context. General-context holds alloc/free callbacks and user data used by other PCRE2 objects.
requirements: gcontext must be a valid general context previously created by pcre2_general_context_create (or NULL if copying a default is allowed; not stated in header).
Returned context must be freed with pcre2_general_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_general_context_create
functions.description: Creates a general allocation context that supplies custom allocation and free callbacks (and an opaque user pointer) for PCRE2 operations that use this context.
requirements: malloc_func and free_func must be function pointers compatible with the given signatures and must correctly allocate/free memory; both must be callable from PCRE2.
memory_data is an opaque pointer passed back to the callbacks; may be NULL.
The returned context must be freed with pcre2_general_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_general_context_free
functions.description: Frees a general-context previously created or copied.
requirements: gcontext must be a context returned by pcre2_general_context_create or pcre2_general_context_copy.
Do not use gcontext after freeing.

functions.name: pcre2_compile_context_copy
functions.description: Copies an existing compile-context. A compile-context stores options and resources used during pattern compilation.
requirements: ccontext must be a valid compile-context previously created by pcre2_compile_context_create (or NULL if allowed; not stated).
Returned context must be freed with pcre2_compile_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_compile_context_create
functions.description: Creates a new compile-context, optionally using a provided general-context for allocations.
requirements: gcontext may be NULL for default allocation or must be a valid pcre2_general_context.
The returned compile-context must be freed with pcre2_compile_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_compile_context_free
functions.description: Frees a compile-context created or copied.
requirements: ccontext must be a valid compile-context from PCRE2.
Do not use ccontext after freeing.

functions.name: pcre2_set_bsr
functions.description: Sets the backslash-R (\R) interpretation mode in a compile-context (Unicode vs ANYCRLF).
requirements: ccontext must be a valid compile-context.
bsr must be one of PCRE2_BSR_UNICODE or PCRE2_BSR_ANYCRLF.
Check return code for success.

functions.name: pcre2_set_character_tables
functions.description: Supplies custom character tables (e.g., for character classes) to a compile-context.
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
tables must point to a valid PCRE2 character tables block as produced by pcre2_maketables or compatible; pointer must remain valid as required by PCRE2 (exact lifetime unspecified in header).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_compile_extra_options
functions.description: Sets additional compile-time behavior flags on the compile-context (PCRE2_EXTRA_*).
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
extra_options is a bitmask of PCRE2_EXTRA_* flags defined in the header.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_max_pattern_length
functions.description: Sets a limit on the maximum length (in code units) of the source pattern that can be compiled using this compile-context.
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
max_length is a size (PCRE2_SIZE); ranges and special values are not documented in the header.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_max_pattern_compiled_length
functions.description: Sets a limit on the size of the compiled pattern code generated during compilation when using this compile-context.
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
max_compiled_length is a size in bytes/code units (unspecified in header).
Check return code.

functions.name: pcre2_set_max_varlookbehind
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed variable-length lookbehind length for patterns compiled with this compile-context.
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
max_code_units is the maximum number of code units; acceptable range not documented here.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_newline
functions.description: Sets the newline convention for pattern compilation and matching behavior (e.g., CR, LF, CRLF, ANY, ANYCRLF, NUL).
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
newline must be one of PCRE2_NEWLINE_* constants.
Check return code.

functions.name: pcre2_set_parens_nest_limit
functions.description: Sets the maximum parentheses nesting depth allowed during compilation.
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
limit is a positive nesting limit; exact bounds not specified here.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_compile_recursion_guard
functions.description: Installs a callback that PCRE2 calls during compilation to guard against excessive recursion; the callback can decide whether to continue.
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
guard must be a valid function pointer taking (uint32_t depth, void *user_data) and returning an int; semantics not specified here.
user_data is passed back to the guard; may be NULL.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_optimize
functions.description: Sets optimization directives for compilation behavior (e.g., enable/disable specific optimizations).
requirements: ccontext must be valid.
directive must be one of PCRE2_OPTIMIZATION_* and related values listed (e.g., PCRE2_OPTIMIZATION_FULL, PCRE2_AUTO_POSSESS, etc.).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_match_context_copy
functions.description: Copies a match-context which stores limits, callouts, and JIT stack assignment for matching operations.
requirements: mcontext must be a valid match-context.
Returned context must be freed with pcre2_match_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_match_context_create
functions.description: Creates a new match-context, optionally using a supplied general-context for allocation.
requirements: gcontext may be NULL or a valid pcre2_general_context.
Returned context must be freed with pcre2_match_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_match_context_free
functions.description: Frees a match-context created or copied.
requirements: mcontext must be a valid match-context.
Do not use mcontext after freeing.

functions.name: pcre2_set_callout
functions.description: Registers a match-time callout function and opaque data in the match-context. PCRE2 invokes the callback at callout points in the pattern.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
callout must be a function pointer matching the signature; may be NULL to remove (not specified here).
callout_data is passed to the callback; may be NULL.
Callback must tolerate being called many times and must not longjmp/throw across PCRE2 unless documented.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_substitute_callout
functions.description: Registers a callout for substitution processing (used by pcre2_substitute).
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
callout must be a valid function pointer with the given signature; may be NULL to disable (not specified here).
callout_data is opaque and passed back.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_substitute_case_callout
functions.signature: int pcre2_set_substitute_case_callout(pcre2_match_context *mcontext, PCRE2_SIZE (*case_callout)(PCRE2_SPTR in, PCRE2_SIZE in_len, PCRE2_UCHAR *out, PCRE2_SIZE out_size, int type, void *data), void *callout_data);
functions.description: Registers a case-conversion callout used by substitution with case transformations, allowing custom case mapping of replacement text.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
case_callout must match the specified signature and handle the indicated type values (PCRE2_SUBSTITUTE_CASE_*).
out buffer size and return semantics are not documented here; follow PCRE2 docs.
callout_data is passed through.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_depth_limit
functions.description: Sets the maximum backtracking/recursion depth during matching.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
limit must be a non-negative limit; exact range not specified.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_heap_limit
functions.description: Sets a limit on heap memory usage during matching.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
limit is a limit value; exact units unspecified in header.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_match_limit
functions.description: Sets the match limit (e.g., maximum number of internal match operations) to constrain matching time/complexity.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
limit must be in an acceptable range (unspecified here).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_offset_limit
functions.description: Sets the offset limit for matching operations, constraining how far into the subject PCRE2 may look.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
limit is a size in code units; semantics not fully specified here.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_recursion_limit
functions.description: Obsolete synonym for setting depth/recursion limit; kept for backward compatibility. In this header it aliases pcre2_set_recursion_limit_.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
limit must be within allowed range (unspecified).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_recursion_memory_management
functions.signature: int pcre2_set_recursion_memory_management(pcre2_match_context *mcontext, void *(*malloc_func)(size_t, void *), void (*free_func)(void *, void *), void *memory_data);
functions.description: Obsolete function retained for backward compatibility; now a no-op according to the header comment.
requirements: mcontext must be valid (though the function is a no-op).
Callbacks may be ignored by the library; callers should not rely on this to change behavior.
Check return value; behavior unspecified.

functions.name: pcre2_convert_context_copy
functions.description: Copies a convert-context used for pattern source conversions (e.g., POSIX/glob to PCRE).
requirements: cvcontext must be valid.
Returned context must be freed with pcre2_convert_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_convert_context_create
functions.description: Creates a new convert-context, optionally using a supplied general-context for allocation.
requirements: gcontext may be NULL or a valid general-context.
Returned context must be freed with pcre2_convert_context_free.

functions.name: pcre2_convert_context_free
functions.description: Frees a convert-context created or copied.
requirements: cvcontext must be valid.
Do not use cvcontext after freeing.

functions.name: pcre2_set_glob_escape
functions.description: Sets the escape character/code point to be used when converting glob patterns.
requirements: cvcontext must be valid.
code_point is a code point value; valid range not specified here.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_set_glob_separator
functions.description: Sets the path separator code point to be used for glob conversions.
requirements: cvcontext must be valid.
code_point value must be an intended separator; exact constraints not specified.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_compile
functions.signature: pcre2_code *pcre2_compile(PCRE2_SPTR pattern, PCRE2_SIZE pattern_length, uint32_t options, int *errorcode, PCRE2_SIZE *erroroffset, pcre2_compile_context *ccontext);
functions.description: Compiles a pattern string into a pcre2_code object using the specified options and compile-context. On error, returns NULL and sets error code and offset.
requirements: pattern must point to a valid pattern string in the library’s code unit width; may be zero-terminated if pattern_length == PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
pattern_length must be the length in code units or PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
options is a bitmask of PCRE2_* compile options (as documented above).
errorcode must be non-NULL if you need the reason for failure; may be NULL if you ignore detailed errors (unspecified).
erroroffset must be non-NULL if you need the offset of the error; may be NULL if you ignore it (unspecified).
ccontext may be NULL for defaults or a valid compile-context.
Returned pcre2_code must be freed with pcre2_code_free.

functions.name: pcre2_code_free
functions.description: Frees a compiled pattern object created by pcre2_compile or its copy functions.
requirements: code must be a valid pointer returned by pcre2_compile or copy functions.
Do not use code after freeing.

functions.name: pcre2_code_copy
functions.description: Creates a duplicate of a compiled pattern object, sharing or copying internal resources as defined by PCRE2.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
Returned code must be freed with pcre2_code_free.

functions.name: pcre2_code_copy_with_tables
functions.description: Copies a compiled pattern, ensuring any required character tables are included so the copy can be used without external tables.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
Returned code must be freed with pcre2_code_free.

functions.name: pcre2_pattern_info
functions.signature: int pcre2_pattern_info(const pcre2_code *code, uint32_t what, void *where);
functions.description: Retrieves information about a compiled pattern (e.g., capture count, first code unit). The item requested is selected by what and written to where.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
what must be one of the PCRE2_INFO_* constants.
where must point to writable storage appropriate for the requested item’s type/size (unspecified in header).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_callout_enumerate
functions.signature: int pcre2_callout_enumerate(const pcre2_code *code, int (*callback)(pcre2_callout_enumerate_block *, void *), void *user_data);
functions.description: Iterates over callout points compiled into a pattern and invokes callback with a description block for each.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called potentially multiple times.
user_data is passed through; may be NULL.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_match_data_create
functions.description: Allocates a match-data block to receive match results (ovector and related data).
requirements: ovecsize is the number of capturing pairs to allocate in the ovector (number of pairs); acceptable range not specified here.
gcontext may be NULL or a valid general-context.
Returned match-data must be freed with pcre2_match_data_free.

functions.name: pcre2_match_data_create_from_pattern
functions.description: Allocates match-data sized appropriately for the given compiled pattern’s capture count.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
gcontext may be NULL or valid.
Returned match-data must be freed with pcre2_match_data_free.

functions.name: pcre2_match_data_free
functions.description: Frees a match-data block previously allocated.
requirements: match_data must be valid.
Do not use match_data after freeing.

functions.name: pcre2_dfa_match
functions.signature: int pcre2_dfa_match(const pcre2_code *code, PCRE2_SPTR subject, PCRE2_SIZE length, PCRE2_SIZE start_offset, uint32_t options, pcre2_match_data *match_data, pcre2_match_context *mcontext, int *workspace, PCRE2_SIZE wscount);
functions.description: Performs a DFA-based match of a compiled pattern against a subject string, storing results in match_data. Requires a caller-supplied workspace array.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
subject must point to valid input in the library’s code unit width; may be zero-terminated if length == PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
length is the subject length or PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
start_offset must be within [0, length].
options is a bitmask of PCRE2_* match/dfa options (see header).
match_data must be a valid match-data block.
mcontext may be NULL or a valid match-context.
workspace must point to an array of int with at least wscount elements; appropriate size depends on pattern/usage (not specified here).
Check return value for match count or negative error codes.

functions.name: pcre2_match
functions.signature: int pcre2_match(const pcre2_code *code, PCRE2_SPTR subject, PCRE2_SIZE length, PCRE2_SIZE start_offset, uint32_t options, pcre2_match_data *match_data, pcre2_match_context *mcontext);
functions.description: Performs a standard backtracking match of a compiled pattern against a subject string, producing captured substring offsets in match_data.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
subject must be valid; may be zero-terminated if length == PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
length is subject length or PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
start_offset must be within [0, length].
options is a bitmask of PCRE2_* match options.
match_data must be valid and large enough for captures (use create_from_pattern to size correctly).
mcontext may be NULL or valid.
Check return value for number of captures set or negative error codes (e.g., PCRE2_ERROR_NOMATCH).

functions.name: pcre2_get_mark
functions.description: Returns the subject pointer to the most recent MARK name (or NULL) set during the last match stored in match_data.
requirements: match_data must be a valid match-data containing results from the most recent match call.
Return value may be NULL if no MARK was set.

functions.name: pcre2_get_match_data_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the match-data block.
requirements: match_data must be valid.

functions.name: pcre2_get_match_data_heapframes_size
functions.description: Returns the size of heap frames within the match-data (used internally for backtracking frames).
requirements: match_data must be valid.

functions.name: pcre2_get_ovector_count
functions.description: Returns the number of offset pairs (ovector slots) available/set in the match-data.
requirements: match_data must be valid.

functions.name: pcre2_get_ovector_pointer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the ovector array (pairs of start/end offsets) in the match-data.
requirements: match_data must be valid.
The returned pointer remains valid while match_data is alive and not modified by other calls that may reallocate.

functions.name: pcre2_get_startchar
functions.description: Returns the starting subject offset from which the most recent match attempt in match_data began (useful for resuming after partials).
requirements: match_data must be valid.

functions.name: pcre2_next_match
functions.description: Convenience function to find the next match in the same subject using stored state in match_data; updates start_offset/options as needed.
requirements: match_data must hold the result/state of a previous match on a subject.
start_offset must point to a writable PCRE2_SIZE where the next search start offset will be read/updated.
options must point to writable options flags used/updated for the next search.
Check return value for match count or error code.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_copy_byname
functions.description: Copies the substring captured by the named group into caller-supplied buffer, updating bufflen with the length used/required.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
name must point to the group name (zero-terminated in the library’s width; unspecified here).
buffer must point to writable storage; may be NULL to query size (unspecified).
bufflen must point to a PCRE2_SIZE that on input gives buffer capacity and on output receives used/needed length; semantics per PCRE2 docs.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_copy_bynumber
functions.description: Copies the substring captured by the numbered group into buffer.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
number must be a valid capture number present in the pattern.
buffer and bufflen usage follow the same conventions as byname.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_free
functions.description: Frees a substring buffer allocated by the library (e.g., from substring_get_*).
requirements: pointer must be a pointer returned by PCRE2 substring allocation functions.
Do not free with standard free; use this function.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_get_byname
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new buffer containing the substring captured by the named group; returns its length.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
name must identify an existing named capture.
bufferptr must be a writable pointer to receive the allocated buffer; free with pcre2_substring_free.
bufflen must be a writable pointer to receive the substring length.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_get_bynumber
functions.description: Allocates and returns the substring captured by the numbered group.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
number must be a valid capture number.
bufferptr and bufflen must be writable; free buffer with pcre2_substring_free.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_length_byname
functions.description: Returns the length of the substring captured by the named group without copying it.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
name must identify an existing named capture.
lengthptr must be writable.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_length_bynumber
functions.description: Returns the length of a numbered captured substring.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
number must be valid.
lengthptr must be writable.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_nametable_scan
functions.signature: int pcre2_substring_nametable_scan(const pcre2_code *code, PCRE2_SPTR name, PCRE2_SPTR *firstptr, PCRE2_SPTR *lastptr);
functions.description: Searches the compiled pattern’s name table for a given name and returns pointers to the first and last entries matching that name.
requirements: code must be valid.
name must be a valid group name string.
firstptr and lastptr must be writable pointers to receive results (may be NULL if unused; unspecified).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_number_from_name
functions.description: Looks up the capture number associated with a named group in the compiled pattern.
requirements: code must be valid.
name must be a valid group name string.
Check return value; returns capture number or error.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_list_free
functions.description: Frees a list of substrings previously obtained by pcre2_substring_list_get.
requirements: list must be a pointer returned by pcre2_substring_list_get.
Do not free with standard free.

functions.name: pcre2_substring_list_get
functions.description: Returns all captured substrings as a newly allocated list of pointers and their lengths.
requirements: match_data must be from a successful match.
listptr and lengthsptr must be writable; free the list with pcre2_substring_list_free.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_serialize_encode
functions.signature: int32_t pcre2_serialize_encode(const pcre2_code **codes, int32_t number_of_codes, uint8_t **serialized_bytes, PCRE2_SIZE *serialized_size, pcre2_general_context *gcontext);
functions.description: Serializes one or more compiled patterns into a single byte block for storage or transport.
requirements: codes must point to an array of valid compiled pattern pointers of length number_of_codes.
number_of_codes must be non-negative and reflect the number of codes.
serialized_bytes must be a writable pointer to receive the allocated byte block; free with pcre2_serialize_free.
serialized_size must be writable to receive the size in bytes.
gcontext may be NULL or valid.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_serialize_decode
functions.signature: int32_t pcre2_serialize_decode(pcre2_code **codes, int32_t number_of_codes, const uint8_t *serialized_bytes, pcre2_general_context *gcontext);
functions.description: Deserializes a byte block produced by pcre2_serialize_encode into compiled pattern objects.
requirements: codes must point to storage for number_of_codes pcre2_code* outputs (or NULL to count? not stated).
number_of_codes must match the number encoded or be large enough (consult docs).
serialized_bytes must point to a valid serialized buffer.
gcontext may be NULL or valid.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_serialize_get_number_of_codes
functions.description: Returns the number of compiled patterns contained in a serialized byte block.
requirements: serialized_bytes must point to a valid serialized buffer produced by pcre2_serialize_encode.

functions.name: pcre2_serialize_free
functions.description: Frees a serialized byte block allocated by pcre2_serialize_encode.
requirements: serialized_bytes must be a pointer returned by pcre2_serialize_encode.
Do not free with standard free.

functions.name: pcre2_substitute
functions.signature: int pcre2_substitute(const pcre2_code *code, PCRE2_SPTR subject, PCRE2_SIZE length, PCRE2_SIZE start_offset, uint32_t options, pcre2_match_data *match_data, pcre2_match_context *mcontext, PCRE2_SPTR replacement, PCRE2_SIZE replacement_length, PCRE2_UCHAR *outbuf, PCRE2_SIZE *outlengthptr);
functions.description: Performs match-and-substitute on the subject using the compiled pattern and replacement template, writing the result to the output buffer.
requirements: code must be valid.
subject must be valid; length may be PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
start_offset within [0, length].
options is a bitmask of PCRE2_SUBSTITUTE_* and match options permitted for substitute (see header).
match_data must be valid.
mcontext may be NULL or valid (and may carry substitute callouts).
replacement must point to a replacement template; replacement_length may be PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
outbuf must be a writable buffer; outlengthptr must point to its size on input and receive the output size/needed length (semantics per PCRE2 docs).
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_pattern_convert
functions.signature: int pcre2_pattern_convert(PCRE2_SPTR pattern, PCRE2_SIZE length, uint32_t options, PCRE2_UCHAR **converted, PCRE2_SIZE *converted_length, pcre2_convert_context *cvcontext);
functions.description: Converts a pattern in an alternate syntax (e.g., POSIX basic/extended, glob) into a PCRE2 pattern string based on options.
requirements: pattern must be valid; length may be PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED.
options is a bitmask of PCRE2_CONVERT_* flags.
converted must be a writable pointer to receive the allocated converted pattern; free with pcre2_converted_pattern_free.
converted_length must be writable to receive length.
cvcontext may be NULL or valid.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_converted_pattern_free
functions.description: Frees a converted pattern string allocated by pcre2_pattern_convert.
requirements: converted must be a pointer returned by pcre2_pattern_convert.
Do not free with standard free.

functions.name: pcre2_jit_compile
functions.description: JIT-compiles a compiled pattern for faster matching, according to the specified JIT options.
requirements: code must be a valid compiled pattern.
options must be a combination of PCRE2_JIT_* flags.
Check return value; errors such as PCRE2_ERROR_JIT_UNSUPPORTED may occur.

functions.name: pcre2_jit_match
functions.signature: int pcre2_jit_match(const pcre2_code *code, PCRE2_SPTR subject, PCRE2_SIZE length, PCRE2_SIZE start_offset, uint32_t options, pcre2_match_data *match_data, pcre2_match_context *mcontext);
functions.description: Runs a JIT-compiled match. Similar to pcre2_match but uses JIT engine. Some sanity checks (like NO_UTF_CHECK) may be ignored as noted.
requirements: code should have been JIT-compiled; otherwise may fall back or fail (unspecified here).
subject/length/start_offset/options/match_data/mcontext requirements are as for pcre2_match.
Check return value.

functions.name: pcre2_jit_free_unused_memory
functions.description: Asks JIT to free cached/unused memory. May use provided general-context for allocation behavior.
requirements: gcontext may be NULL or valid.

functions.name: pcre2_jit_stack_create
functions.description: Creates a JIT stack object with initial and maximum sizes for use by JIT matching.
requirements: startsize and maxsize specify stack sizes; must be sensible values (unspecified).
gcontext may be NULL or valid.
Returned stack must be freed with pcre2_jit_stack_free.

functions.name: pcre2_jit_stack_assign
functions.description: Assigns a JIT stack to a match-context, either a fixed stack or via a callback that supplies stacks to threads on demand.
requirements: mcontext must be valid.
callback may be NULL or a function of type pcre2_jit_callback that returns a pcre2_jit_stack*; semantics per PCRE2 docs.
callback_data is passed to the callback.
If using a fixed stack, use a callback that returns the desired stack.

functions.name: pcre2_jit_stack_free
functions.description: Frees a JIT stack previously created.
requirements: jit_stack must be a valid JIT stack pointer.
Do not use jit_stack after freeing.

requirements: errorcode must be a PCRE2 error code from the defined ranges.
buffer must point to writable storage of size bufflen code units.

functions.name: pcre2_maketables

functions.name: pcre2_maketables_free

functions.name: pcre2_regcomp
functions.signature: int pcre2_regcomp(regex_t *preg, const char *pattern, int cflags);
functions.description: POSIX wrapper: compiles a POSIX regular expression pattern into a regex_t using PCRE2’s engine.
requirements: preg must point to a valid regex_t to receive compiled data; it will later be freed with pcre2_regfree.
pattern must be a NUL-terminated C string.
cflags is a bitmask of REG_* flags defined in pcre2posix.h (e.g., REG_ICASE, REG_NEWLINE, REG_UTF, etc.).

data_types.description: A pattern string intended for PCRE2 compilation. May contain regex metacharacters, escapes, character classes, Unicode sequences, named capture groups, and options embedded via (?...). It is treated as a byte sequence in the library’s configured code unit width and need not be NUL-terminated when length is provided.
An unconstrained byte buffer used as a subject string for matching. It may contain any bytes, including NUL, non-printable characters, or invalid UTF sequences. Length is provided explicitly.

A short name string used to reference a named capture group. Typically consists of letters, digits, and underscores, and is NUL-terminated. Lengths here are small (up to ~32 bytes). Non-matching names are allowed; APIs may return not-found.

A replacement string used by PCRE2 substitution that may include literal text and special sequences like $1, ${name}, and case-conversion tokens depending on options. Treated as a byte sequence with explicit length.

An input pattern written in an alternate syntax (e.g., POSIX basic/extended or glob) meant for conversion into a PCRE-compatible pattern. It is a general text buffer containing the source notation, passed with explicit length.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# Generator for PCRE2 subject strings (arbitrary byte strings)
# Goals:
# - Produce non-empty byte buffers (fuzzer bails on empty)
# - Include diverse content to exercise regex engines: ASCII words, digits, whitespace,
#   newline variants, NULs, valid UTF-8 multi-byte sequences, long runs, punctuation,
#   path-like, email-like, JSON-like, CSV-like, repeated patterns, mixed case.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Reusable building blocks
ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"hello", b"world", b"Test", b"CamelCase", b"snake_case", b"kebab-case",
    b"foo", b"bar", b"baz", b"qux", b"alpha", b"beta", b"gamma", b"delta",
]
DIGITS = [bytes(str(i), 'ascii') for i in range(10)]
WHITES = [b" ", b"\t", b"\v", b"\f"]
NEWLINES = [b"\n", b"\r", b"\r\n", b"\x00"]  # include NUL as newline-like edge
# ASCII punctuation (including backslash and quote safely encoded)
PUNCT = [
    b"!", b"@", b"#", b"$", b"%", b"^", b"&", b"*", b"(", b")",
    b"[", b"]", b"{", b"}", b"<", b">", b".", b"?", b"+", b"*",
    b"|", b"^", b"$", b"\\", b"'", b'"', b"-", b"_", b"=", b":" , b";", b",", b"/"
]
HEX = [bytes(h, 'ascii') for h in list("0123456789abcdef")]

# Some valid UTF-8 sequences (multi-byte)
UTF8_VALID = [
    "π", "λ", "汉", "字", "🙂", "é", "ñ", "ø", "€", "Ω", "Ђ", "क", "あ", "🧪"
]
UTF8_VALID_BYTES = [s.encode('utf-8') for s in UTF8_VALID]

# Interesting sequences for regex engines
SPECIAL_SEQS = [
    b"A" * 64,
    b"0" * 128,
    b"\x00" * 16,
    b"\xff" * 16,
    b"abcabcabcabcabcabcabcabc",
    b"abababababababababababab",
    b"\n" * 32,
    b"\r\n" * 16,
    b" " + b"\t" + (b" \t" * 8),
]

# Structured snippets
STRUCTURED = [
    b"GET /path/resource?id=123&ok=true HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n",
    b"{\"name\":\"Alice\",\"age\":30,\"tags\":[\"x\",\"y\"]}",
    b"id,name,score\n1,Alice,10\n2,Bob,20\n",
    b"/usr/local/bin:/bin:/usr/bin:/sbin",
    b"user.name+tag@example-domain.test",
    b"C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\etc\\hosts\r\n",
]

# Random bytes helper

def random_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def mix_chunks(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    starters = [
        b"The quick brown fox jumps over 13 lazy dogs.",
        b"email:test@example.com; ip:192.168.0.1; date:2025-01-23",
        b"path:/var/log/app.log; user:alice; uid:1001",
        b"price=$12.34 qty=56 total=$691.04",
    ]
    chunks.append(rng.choice(starters))

    # Add a newline convention run
    chunks.append(rng.choice(NEWLINES) * rng.randint(1, 8))

    # Add ASCII words and digits
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        pieces = [rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS), b" ", rng.choice(DIGITS), rng.choice(WHITES)]
        chunks.append(b"".join(pieces))

    # Add some UTF-8 sequences, interleaved with punctuation
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
        chunks.append(rng.choice(UTF8_VALID_BYTES))
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            chunks.append(rng.choice(PUNCT))

    # Insert structured snippet
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(rng.choice(STRUCTURED))

    # Repetition blocks
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        base = rng.choice([b"abc", b"123", b"xyz", b"Aa", b"( )", b"[]", b"<>", b"\t "]) \
               + (rng.choice(PUNCT) if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"")
        rep = rng.randint(3, 40)
        chunks.append(base * rep)

    # Hex-looking run
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        chunks.append(b"0x" + b"".join(rng.choice(HEX) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 64))))

    # Add special sequences
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        chunks.append(rng.choice(SPECIAL_SEQS))

    # Sprinkle random bytes including NULs
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        chunks.append(random_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 64)))

    # End with newline variant to exercise anchors
    chunks.append(rng.choice(NEWLINES))

    data = b"".join(chunks)

    if len(data) > target_len:
        data = data[:target_len]

    if not data:
        data = b"A\n"

    return data


def choose_target_len(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor medium sizes, but sometimes small or large
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.2:
        return rng.randint(1, 64)
    elif p < 0.8:
        return rng.randint(64, 1024)
    else:
        return rng.randint(1024, min(4096, 3072))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    target_len = choose_target_len(rng)
    data = mix_chunks(rng, target_len)

    # With some probability, craft newline-focused content to trigger \R and newline settings
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        nl_block = rng.choice([
            b"Line1\nLine2\nLine3\n",
            b"CR_only\rCR_only\r",
            b"CRLF_one\r\nCRLF_two\r\n",
            b"NUL_sep\x00A\x00B\x00C\x00",
        ])
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            data = (nl_block + data)[:target_len]
        else:
            remain = max(0, target_len - len(data))
            data = data + nl_block[:remain]

    if len(data) == 0:
        data = b"X"

    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]

    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: alphanumeric identifier
# - NUL-terminated C string
# - Allowed chars: letters, digits, underscore
# - Length: small (<= 32 bytes typical in stubs)
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain group names for APIs that
#   operate on named capture groups. Non-existing names are acceptable.
# Goal: Produce interesting, valid identifiers that exercise different
#   name-table lookup paths: existing-like, edge lengths, case mixes,
#   underscores, leading digits (allowed by PCRE2 with VERNAME rules in
#   many builds), and common group naming patterns like "name", "_",
#   "g1", "CAP1", etc.
# Buffer format: Just one NUL-terminated string, since each stub pulls a
#   single FUZZ_PARAM_STR per call site. The harness typically maps the
#   single input buffer to successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR requests, or reuses
#   the same contents; we therefore emit a single identifier.

MAX_LEN = 32

ALPHA = string.ascii_letters
ALNUMUS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"

COMMON_NAMES: List[str] = [
    "name", "Name", "NAME", "id", "ID", "user", "User", "group", "Group",
    "_", "__", "a", "A", "z", "Z",
    "g1", "g01", "g10", "cap", "cap1", "cap_1", "CAP1",
    "m", "m0", "m1", "match", "sub", "sub1",
    "x", "y", "z1",
]

EDGE_NAMES: List[str] = [
    # Edge cases: max length, leading underscore, digits, alternating case
    "a" * 31,
    "_" * 31,
    "A1" * 15 + "B",           # length 31
    "n" * 32,                   # 32 chars
    "Z9_" * 10 + "x",          # 31
    "0" * 10 + "a" * 10 + "_x", # mixed, <=32
]


def _random_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a strategy: common, edge, or random
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.40 and COMMON_NAMES:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)
    if choice < 0.55 and EDGE_NAMES:
        return rng.choice(EDGE_NAMES)

    # Otherwise generate a random valid identifier (1..32 chars)
    # Allow leading digit or underscore as PCRE2 names accept alphnum+underscore
    # (PCRE2 generally accepts [A-Za-z0-9_]+ for group names).
    length = rng.randint(1, MAX_LEN)

    # Bias to include underscores and digits
    chars = []
    for i in range(length):
        p = rng.random()
        if p < 0.20:
            chars.append('_')
        elif p < 0.50:
            chars.append(rng.choice(string.digits))
        else:
            # Mix case letters
            c = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)
            if rng.random() < 0.4:
                c = c.upper()
            chars.append(c)
    return ''.join(chars)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    name = _random_identifier(rng)

    # Ensure maximum size constraint (<=32) respected and NUL-terminate for C APIs
    if len(name) > MAX_LEN:
        name = name[:MAX_LEN]

    # Return a single NUL-terminated string buffer
    return (name + "\x00").encode("ascii", errors="ignore")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for PCRE2 replacement template bytes suitable for pcre2_substitute.
# Buffer layout:
#   [len_subj (2 bytes LE)] [subj bytes]
#   [len_repl (2 bytes LE)] [repl bytes]
# Keep total <= 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_SUBJ = 1024
MAX_REPL = 128  # stub truncates to 128 anyway

# Interesting building blocks for subjects and replacement templates
WORD_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"
PUNCT = "-._:/@#&=+*,;!?\'\"()[]{}|^$`~"
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    " café ",
    "naïve",
    "Δx=π",
    "汉字",
    "🙂👍",
    "ßstraße",
    "mañana",
]

# Common replacement tokens for PCRE2 ($-style)
BASIC_CAPS = ["$0", "$1", "$2", "$3", "$9"]
NAMED_EXAMPLES = ["${name}", "${word}", "${_}", "${Group}"]

    "\\E",  # end case

]

LITERALS = ["-", "_", ".", ",", ":", "/", " "]

# Some subject patterns that interact with replacement features
SUBJECT_TEMPLATES = [
    "hello world",

    "line1\nline2\nline3",
    "email: user@example.com",
    "tags: alpha beta gamma",
    "(cap) [groups] {test}",

] + UNICODE_SAMPLES

# Replacement recipes that exercise features but should still be valid
REPLACEMENT_RECIPES = [
    "$0",

    "${name}",

    "\\U$0\\E",

    "\\u$1",
    "\\l$1",
    "$1-\\n-$2",
    "[$0]",
    "${_}",
    "${Group}",
]

# Build a subject with optional interesting characters
def build_subject(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        base = rng.choice(SUBJECT_TEMPLATES)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Mixed words and punctuation
        parts: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
            wlen = rng.randint(1, 8)
            word = ''.join(rng.choice(WORD_CHARS) for _ in range(wlen))
            parts.append(word)
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                parts.append(rng.choice(LITERALS + list(PUNCT)))
        base = ''.join(parts)
    elif choice == 2:
        # Include whitespace and newlines
        lines: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
            wlen = rng.randint(3, 10)
            word = ''.join(rng.choice(WORD_CHARS) for _ in range(wlen))
            lines.append(word)
        base = '\n'.join(lines)
    elif choice == 3:
        # Unicode-heavy string
        base = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES) + " " + rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    else:
        # Structured key=value list
        items: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
            key = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(3,6)))
            val = ''.join(rng.choice(WORD_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,6)))
            items.append(f"{key}={val}")
        base = '; '.join(items)

    # Trim to max_len but ensure non-empty
    if not base:
        base = "x"
    if len(base) > max_len:
        base = base[:max_len]
    return base

# Build a PCRE2 replacement template
def build_replacement(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Optionally add a case scope prefix
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(rng.choice(["\\U", "\\L"]))
    # Add several components
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)):
        kind = rng.random()
        if kind < 0.25:
            parts.append(rng.choice(BASIC_CAPS))
        elif kind < 0.45:
            parts.append(rng.choice(NAMED_EXAMPLES))
        elif kind < 0.65:
            # literal run
            run_chars = WORD_CHARS + WHITESPACE + PUNCT
            run = ''.join(rng.choice(run_chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
            parts.append(run)
        elif kind < 0.8:
            parts.append(rng.choice(CASE_TOKENS))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(ESCAPES))
    # Optionally close case scope
    if any(tok in parts for tok in ("\\U", "\\L")):
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            parts.append("\\E")
    # Also mix a pre-made recipe sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        insert_pos = rng.randint(0, len(parts))
        parts.insert(insert_pos, rng.choice(REPLACEMENT_RECIPES))

    s = ''.join(parts)
    if not s:
        s = "$0"
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s


def pack_lengths_and_strings(subj: bytes, repl: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 2-byte little-endian lengths
    ls = len(subj)
    lr = len(repl)
    if ls > 0xFFFF:
        subj = subj[:0xFFFF]
        ls = len(subj)
    if lr > 0xFFFF:
        repl = repl[:0xFFFF]
        lr = len(repl)
    return ls.to_bytes(2, 'little') + subj + lr.to_bytes(2, 'little') + repl


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    subj_max = min(MAX_SUBJ, MAX_TOTAL // 2)
    repl_max = min(MAX_REPL, MAX_TOTAL // 2)

    subj = build_subject(rng, subj_max)
    if not subj:
        subj = "x"

    repl = build_replacement(rng, repl_max)

    subj_b = subj.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    repl_b = repl.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')

    out = pack_lengths_and_strings(subj_b, repl_b)
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        trim = MAX_TOTAL - 4  # keep headers
        subj_b = subj_b[: max(0, trim // 2)]
        repl_b = repl_b[: max(0, trim - len(subj_b))]
        out = pack_lengths_and_strings(subj_b, repl_b)
    return out
